title: Orders per Month
statement:
Count how many orders a shop received in each calendar month.

The `orders` table has one row per order: `id` (integer), `customer` (text), `ordered_at` (timestamp, when the order was placed), and `total` (numeric, the order amount). The orders can span more than one year.

Return one row per month that has at least one order, with two columns:

- `month`: the month as text in the form `YYYY-MM`, like `2024-11`
- `order_count`: the number of orders placed in that month

Order the rows by `month`, oldest first.

Expected output:

```text
  month  | order_count
---------+-------------
 2024-11 |           2
 2024-12 |           3
 2025-01 |           2
 2025-03 |           1
(4 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer TEXT NOT NULL,
  ordered_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  total NUMERIC(8, 2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO orders (id, customer, ordered_at, total) VALUES
  (1, 'Ada Lovelace', '2024-11-03 09:15:00', 42.50),
  (2, 'Grace Hopper', '2024-11-18 14:02:00', 18.00),
  (3, 'Alan Turing', '2024-12-01 00:05:00', 75.25),
  (4, 'Ada Lovelace', '2024-12-24 19:40:00', 12.99),
  (5, 'Edsger Dijkstra', '2024-12-31 23:59:00', 30.00),
  (6, 'Grace Hopper', '2025-01-02 08:30:00', 55.10),
  (7, 'Barbara Liskov', '2025-01-15 12:00:00', 21.75),
  (8, 'Alan Turing', '2025-03-09 16:45:00', 99.00);
hints: `to_char` can format a timestamp with a pattern like `'YYYY-MM'`.
Group by the formatted month, so every order in the same month lands in one group.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: format ordered_at as YYYY-MM and count the orders in each month
SELECT ordered_at AS month,
       1 AS order_count
FROM orders
ORDER BY ordered_at, id;
sql.solution:
SELECT to_char(ordered_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
